title: The year in one sitting
hookLine: the poem, the disciples, the songs, the tales, the roads, the teachers, the history
tomorrow: Year three close: the great story

cards: Near the top of a long climb, a hiker stops, turns around, and looks back down the trail. From up there, the switchbacks that felt endless are a few lines on a hillside, and the whole path makes sense at once.
Tomorrow this year closes. So today, before the last step, turn around: one look back over a year that began with a poem and ended with festivals.

teach.b: It began with a poem. Ashvaghosha's Buddhacarita told the life as an epic: the palace, the king's fear, and the old man the gods placed on the prince's road so that he would see. Then the disciples.
Sariputta and Moggallana, the friends who went looking together. Ananda, who remembered. Mahakassapa in his rag robe.
The women who asked to be ordained, and the whole sangha, wise and proud and forgetful, all welcome.
Then the songs of the elders, in their own words: Patacara watching a lamp's wick drawn down until the flame went out, and Mutta, free of the mortar, the pestle and her crooked husband.
Then the Jataka's long tales: Sumedha lying down in the mud so a Buddha of the past could walk across him, and the caravan leader who kept the water when spirits told him to throw it away.
Then the roads: councils where the elders recited the teaching from memory, monks traveling with merchants on the Silk Road, translators like Kumarajiva, and Faxian setting out on foot for India.
Then the teachers: Nagarjuna's middle way, Asanga tending a wounded dog, Shantideva, thought lazy, standing up to recite a long poem on the bodhisattva's way.
Then history, held honestly: monasteries closed and reopened, Cambodia's sangha rebuilt from few, the empty niches at Bamiyan.
And these last days, the festival year: a lamp at Vesak, sweet tea for the baby Buddha, a circle dance, a robe, a week of sitting, a day of miracles.
From up here, the switchbacks were a poem, a song, a tale, a road, a teacher, a hard chapter. Now they're one trail, and you walked all of it.

how: Some Buddhist communities mark the end of a period of study or a retreat with a longer sitting and a review of what was learned, sometimes followed by a dedication of merit.

games.q: you're a caravan leader crossing a desert. spirits on the road tell you there's water ahead, so throw away what you carry. what do you do?
o: throw it away and travel light
send scouts and throw away half
games.why: the leader in the Jataka keeps the water and his caravan comes through. it was one of this year's tales.

practice: Let one picture from this year come back by itself. Don't choose it; take whatever arrives first: a lamp, a bowl, a road, a dog, a robe, a face. Stay with it, and notice what your mind kept when you weren't trying to keep anything.

wordCard.voice: Buddhacarita. The poem that opened this year, now seen whole with the disciples, the songs, the tales, the roads, the teachers, the history, the festivals. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit Buddhacarita: Ashvaghosha's poem of the Buddha's life, where this year began.

carryVoice: Your line: look how far. Every story this year was a step on the same climb. One more day to the top.
